This retired Marine lieutenant colonel and Vietnam veteran devised the plan to divert Iran arms-sale profits to Contra rebels, testifying before Congress under limited immunity — who is he?
Assassinated in 1961, this pan-Africanist served as the first prime minister of the newly independent Congo before the Congo Crisis erupted?
Patrice Lumumba: Congolese politician and independence leader (1925–1961)

Lasting from September 1939 to May 1940, this eight-month lull saw virtually no major Allied land operations on the Western Front despite the outbreak of global hostilities — what was this quiet period called?
Phoney War: Initial period of low activity in World War II.
This Macedonian Greek general, one of Alexander the Great's most trusted companions, retrieved his leader's body after his death and founded a new ruling dynasty in Egypt — who is he?
Ptolemy I Soter: Pharaoh of Egypt from 305 to 282 BC.
Ruling in medieval Delhi from 1236 to 1240, this daughter of Shamsuddin Iltutmish became the only female Muslim monarch to ever hold the throne there — who was she?
Razia Sultan: Raziyyat-Ud-Dunya Wa Ud-Din (Persian: سلطان رضیه الدنیا والدین; c.
The longest-serving prime minister in his nation's history, this Melbourne lawyer led one party in the 1930s and then founded an entirely new one for his second, much longer stint — who was he?
Robert Menzies: Prime Minister of Australia (1939–1941; 1949–1966)
This politician resigned as Kyrgyzstan's acting president in November 2020 just so he could run in — and win — the 2021 election that made him the country's sixth president. Who is he?
Sadyr Japarov: President of Kyrgyzstan since 2021. Japarov returned to Kyrgyzstan in 2017, where he was arrested and sentenced to an 11 year prison term due to his prior illegal political activities.

This early 20th-century youth movement emphasizes outdoor skills like camping and woodcraft, uses a uniform designed to hide social class differences, and awards merit badges bearing a fleur-de-lis. What movement is it?
Scouting: Youth movement. Scouting or the Scout Movement is a youth movement which became popularly established in the first decade of the 20th century.

Head of a leading Naqshbandi religious order in eastern Anatolia, this Zaza Kurdish leader toured the region in 1907 building ties with Hamidiye cavalry officers before leading a 1925 uprising bearing his name — who was he?
Sheikh Said: Kurdish religious leader (1865–1925). Sheikh Said studied religious sciences at the madrasa led by his father Sheikh Mahmud Fevzi as well from several Islamic scholars in the region.
The first pharaoh of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty pioneered new pyramid-building techniques, leaving at least three pyramids still standing today — who was he?
Flourishing along the Tigris and Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia, this is considered the earliest known civilization, home to the world's oldest surviving texts from Uruk — what was it called?
Sumer: Ancient Mesopotamian civilization from 3300 to 1900 BC.

Eldest daughter of a Raiatean king, she became a queen consort of Tahiti through an arranged marriage to a widowed second cousin, then ruled as Queen of Huahine — and even fought in the Battle of Te Feipī. Who was she?
Teriitaria II: Queen of Tahiti and Huahine (c. 1790 – 1858)

The third shōgun of a ruling dynasty, this Japanese leader closed the country's borders to Europeans and persecuted Christians during his 1623-1651 reign, a policy that lasted over two centuries — who is he?
Tokugawa Iemitsu: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military leader of Japan from 1623 to 1651.
With Merlin's magic making him look like his rival Gorlois, this legendary British king slept with Lady Igraine and fathered a certain 'once and future king' — who was he?
Uther Pendragon: Father of King Arthur in Arthurian legend.
As Vice Chair of Russia's State Duma from a liberal-leaning party, he ran in the 2024 presidential election calling for peace negotiations 'without a rollback' — who is he?
Among Queen Victoria's 42 grandchildren he was the eldest, yet he'd preside over the end of his dynasty's 400-year grip on Prussia when he abdicated in 1918 — which last German Emperor?
Wilhelm II: German Emperor from 1888 to 1918.
This Indian politician, who leads the Andhra Pradesh unit of the Congress party, is the daughter of a former chief minister and younger sister of another prominent state politician — who is she?
This authoritarian ruler seized Tunisia's presidency in a bloodless 1987 coup by declaring his predecessor incompetent, then fled to Saudi Arabia when revolution toppled him in 2011 — who was he?
Zine El Abidine Ben Ali: President of Tunisia from 1987 to 2011.
Who among these was born first?
Omar Khayyam (born 1048) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Who among these is a physicist?
Which of these is a mathematician?
Emmy Noether is a mathematician. Amalie Emmy Noether (23 March 1882 – 14 April 1935) was a German mathematician who made many important contributions to abstract algebra.
What is the atomic number of Meitnerium?
Meitnerium: Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
What is the atomic number of Rubidium?
Rubidium: Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
In what year was Pope Benedict XVI born?
Pope Benedict XVI: Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.
In what year was Javier Milei born?
Javier Milei: Javier Gerardo Milei (born 22 October 1970) is an Argentine politician and economist who has served as the 57th president of Argentina since 2023.
In what year was Piero Ferrari born?
Piero Ferrari: Piero Ferrari (born Piero Lardi, 22 May 1945; later Piero Lardi Ferrari) is an Italian billionaire businessman and sport personality.
In what year did Giordano Bruno die?
Giordano Bruno: Bruno's pantheism was not taken lightly by the church, nor was his teaching of metempsychosis regarding the reincarnation of the soul.
In what year did Erwin Schrödinger die?
Erwin Schrödinger: Schrödinger shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac "for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory".
In what year was Silicon discovered?
Silicon: Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
Which company manufactures Antonov An-124 Ruslan?
Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Aviastar-SP. The An-124 remains the largest military transport aircraft in service.
In which country is Mil Mi-8?
Mil Mi-8: Burkina Faso. The Mi-8 is the world's most-produced helicopter, with over 17,000 units used by over 50 countries.
Who is credited with discovering Antlia?
Antlia: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Antlia (from Ancient Greek ἀντλία) is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Factitious disorder imposed on another?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: Roy Meadow. The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
Who is credited with discovering Trisomy 18?
Trisomy 18: John H. Edwards. Trisomy 18, also known as Edwards syndrome, is a genetic disorder.
Who is credited with discovering Strontium?
Strontium: William Cruickshank. Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.
A "classic organochlorine" insecticide once heavily used to treat seed and soil, it was banned in most countries by the 1990s after proving a persistent, bioaccumulating pollutant. What is it?
Aldrin is an organochlorine insecticide that was widely used until the 1990s, when it was banned in most countries.
This deep-tissue swelling — of the face, tongue, throat, or limbs — comes on within minutes to hours and is driven by either histamine or bradykinin — what is it?
Angioedema is an area of swelling (edema) of the lower layer of skin and tissue just under the skin or mucous membranes.
Sharing chemistry with phosphorus and antimony, this group-15 metalloid carries the symbol As and a notorious reputation for toxicity — what is it?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
The second-largest living rodents after capybaras, these large semiaquatic mammals of the Northern Hemisphere have webbed back feet, hand-like front paws, and flat, scaly tails — name the animal?
Beaver (genus Castor) are large semiaquatic rodents of the Northern Hemisphere.
Around 2,500 species of this insect family defend themselves by secreting a skin-irritating toxin called cantharidin, often flaunting bold warning colors — which family?
Blister beetle are beetles of the family Meloidae, so called for their defensive secretion of a blistering agent, cantharidin.

This British dog breed of mastiff type has a stocky build, a large head, thick facial skin folds, and a protruding lower jaw, and is now illegal to breed in the Netherlands over health concerns — name the breed?
Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
Seen as the frontman of Mexican neoliberalism, this economist-president championed and signed NAFTA after an election clouded by fraud accusations — who is he?
Carlos Salinas de Gortari (Spanish; born 3 April 1948) is a Mexican economist and former politician who served as the 60th president of Mexico from 1988 to 1994.
Patented in 1948 and used to treat hay fever and other allergic conditions, this first-generation antihistamine works within two hours by blocking the H1 histamine receptor — name the drug?
Chlorphenamine (CP, CPM), also known as chlorpheniramine, is an antihistamine used to treat the symptoms of allergic conditions such as allergic rhinitis (hay fever).

Ranging across most of Europe and into the Palearctic as far as northwestern China, this medium-sized bird of prey sees its northernmost populations migrate as far as South Africa each winter — which raptor?
Common buzzard (Buteo buteo) is a medium-sized bird of prey with a large range.
Bottle gourds, bitter melon, and the fibrous fruit that gives us loofah sponges are all members of which roughly 965-species plant family?
Cucurbitaceae (kew-), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
Birds are the only surviving lineage of these warmblooded Mesozoic reptiles, having evolved from theropods in the Late Jurassic — what is the broader group called?
Dinosaur are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria.

This is the industrial process of converting other forms of energy into electric power, typically at power plants using electromechanical devices, before it is transmitted and distributed to end users. What is this process called?
Electricity generation is the process of generating electric power from sources of primary energy.

This simple hydrocarbon gas, the simplest member of a class called alkenes, is the most-produced organic compound on Earth by tonnage, and is the primary building block of a common plastic — what is it?
Ethylene (IUPAC name: ethene) is a hydrocarbon which has the formula C2H4 or H2C=CH2.
Using a skin membrane called a patagium plus a long tail for steering, these gliding rodents can sail from tree to tree without true flight — what are they called?
Flying squirrel (scientifically known as Pteromyini or Petauristini) are a tribe of 50 species of squirrels in the family Sciuridae.
Arriving late to a lecture, this mathematician copied down two famous unsolved problems thinking they were homework — and solved them; he's better known for the simplex algorithm, but who was he?

George Dantzig (November 8, 1914 - May 13, 2005) was an American mathematical scientist who made contributions to industrial engineering, operations research, computer science, economics and statistics.
Endemic to Africa and among the oldest of the gallinaceous birds, this family branched off before New World quail evolutionarily — name the birds?
Guinea fowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.

The reciprocal cross to the more common mule, this equine hybrid is the offspring of a male horse and a female donkey, differing from its counterpart in both physiology and temperament — what is it called?
Hinny is a domestic equine hybrid, the offspring of a male horse (a stallion) and a female donkey (a jenny).
First appearing in the fossil record in Egypt some 37 million years ago, this order of small African herbivores once rivaled odd-toed ungulates in size and diversity — which order?
Hyracoidea is a taxonomic order of mammals.
A chemist who studied chlorophyll and once worked on developing poison gases in WWI, he later led Harvard and became the first U.S. Ambassador to West Germany — who was he?
James B. Conant (March 26, 1893 - February 11, 1978) was an American chemist, a President of Harvard University, and the first U.S.
This mammalogist survived a 3,000-meter fall strapped to her airplane seat after a 1971 lightning strike, then spent 11 days alone in the Amazon before rescue — who is she?
Juliane Koepcke (born 10 October 1954), is a German-Peruvian mammalogist who specialises in bats.
Depicted as the goddess Minerva, this Italian physicist became the first woman with a science doctorate and the first salaried female university teacher. Who was she?
Laura Bassi (29 October 1711 - 20 February 1778) was an Italian physicist and academic.
Prized as one of the most profitable seafood commodities in the coastal waters where it's caught, this clawed crustacean spends its life in crevices and burrows on the sea floor - which creature?
Lobster are malacostracan decapod crustaceans of the family Nephropidae or its synonym Homaridae.
Its bell-shaped flowers give way to yellow or orange berries, but this nightshade genus is better known by the folkloric root that inspired countless myths and superstitions — which genus?
Mandragora (genus) is a plant genus belonging to the nightshade family (Solanaceae).
Its three main jobs are converting food into usable energy, building macromolecules like proteins and lipids, and excreting waste — the chemistry that keeps every living thing alive. What is it?
Metabolism (from) refers to the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that occur within living organisms.
Also called Indian mulberry, this tropical fruit tree contains harmful anthraquinones, and its foul-smelling fruit is mostly eaten only as a famine food — which species is it?
Morinda citrifolia is a fruit-bearing tree in the coffee family, Rubiaceae.
First linked by a Michigan doctor to farm wives sickened by isolation, this Gilded Age diagnosis grouped together fatigue, headaches, and a depressed mood — what condition?
Neurasthenia (from Ancient Greek (neuron) 'nerve' and (asthens) 'weak') is a term that was first used as early as 1829 for a mechanical weakness of the nerves.
Concerned with the most fundamental concept of all — being — this branch of metaphysics distinguishes non-repeatable particulars from repeatable universals like 'green' — what is the field?
Ontology is the philosophical study of being.
Named after a 17th-century French mathematician and physicist, this SI unit of pressure is defined as one newton of force per square metre — name the unit?
Pascal (unit) (symbol: Pa) is the unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI).
One of nine essential amino acids we must eat rather than make ourselves, it's found in mammals' milk and acts as a direct precursor to the neuromodulator phenethylamine — which molecule is it?
Phenylalanine (symbol Phe or F) is an -amino acid with the formula C9H11NO2.

This natural process transfers pollen from a flower's anther to its stigma, enabling fertilization and seed production, carried out by everything from bees and bats to wind and water — what process is it?
Pollination is the transfer of pollen from an anther of a plant to the stigma of a plant, later enabling fertilisation and the production of seeds.
Found in more than 200 species of mushroom, this inactive compound is a prodrug your body quickly converts to psilocin, a near-cousin of serotonin — what is it?
Psilocybin (4-), is a naturally occurring tryptamine alkaloid and investigational drug found in more than 200 species of mushrooms, with hallucinogenic and serotonergic effects.
What fat-soluble alcohol form of vitamin A — found in fish, dairy, and meat — is essential for vision, skin maintenance, and immune function, and is used as a supplement to prevent xerophthalmia?
Retinol is a hydrolytic metabolite of retinyl esters belonging to the group of vitamin A1 as an alcohol form.

This zodiac constellation, whose Latin name means 'archer,' is traditionally depicted as a centaur drawing a bow, and its territory in the southern sky contains the center of the Milky Way galaxy. What constellation is this?
Sagittarius (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.
About 90% of the body's supply of this mood-regulating monoamine is actually made in the gut, where it helps drive intestinal movements — which neurotransmitter is it?
Serotonin (5-HT), is a monoamine neurotransmitter with a wide range of functions in both the central nervous system (CNS) and also peripheral tissues.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
Developed from an earlier design, this variable-sweep-wing Soviet fighter-bomber served from 1967 to 1990 and was exported in variants like the Su-22 — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-17 (NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Also called bush crickets, this insect family in the suborder Ensifera includes over 8,000 mostly nocturnal, leaf-mimicking species — which family?
Tettigoniidae are commonly called katydids (especially in North America) or bush crickets.

A phenylpiperazine compound in the serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor class, this antidepressant treats depression, anxiety and insomnia but carries a rare risk of prolonged, painful erections — which drug?
Trazodone is an antidepressant medication used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
Mammals, birds, amphibians, fish, and reptiles all belong to this subphylum of animals, united by a backbone and a braincase — what is it?
Vertebrate are animals with a vertebral column and a cranium.
Though classified as a woodwind, this conical-bodied instrument is usually made of brass and uses a vibrating single reed to produce sound. What instrument is it?
Xoloitzcuintle (or Xoloitzquintle, Xoloitzcuintli, or Xolo) is one of several breeds of hairless dog.
Named for the skull-shaped marking on its thorax and first classified by Carl Linnaeus in 1758, this large moth was immortalized on the poster for 'The Silence of the Lambs' — which insect?
Acherontia atropos: Species of moth. It is most commonly identified by the vaguely skull-shaped pattern adorning the thorax, the characteristic from which its common and scientific names are derived.
Scientifically named Gadus chalcogrammus, this schooling member of the cod family gathers in massive numbers in the eastern Bering Sea — which fish?
Alaska pollock: Species of fish. The Alaska pollock also known as Pacific pollock or walleye pollock (Gadus chalcogrammus) is a marine fish species of the cod genus Gadus and family Gadidae.
Nicknamed 'whip-spiders' or 'tailless whip-scorpions,' these arachnids have no silk, no venom, and a name meaning 'blunt tail' — they grab with their pedipalps instead of biting — what order is this?
Amblypygi: Order of arachnids. The name "amblypygid" means "blunt tail", a reference to a lack of the flagellum that is otherwise seen in whip-scorpions.
Comprising over 22,000 species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches, this phylum of segmented worms use parapodia to move — what is it?
Annelid: Phylum of segmented worms. The basic annelid form consists of multiple segments called metameres.
Known commonly as palms, this family of over 2,600 flowering plant species includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms mostly found in the tropics — what's the family called?
Arecaceae: Palm family of flowering plants.

Also called the moon jellyfish, this once-thought-cosmopolitan species was split into roughly 28 separate species in the 2020s and is now known to live only in the north Atlantic and off Argentina — which species?
Aurelia aurita: Species of jellyfish. The species now identified as A. aurita is only found in the north Atlantic and in Argentina, and is not dangerous to humans.

This single-engine turboprop trainer, a license-built version of the Swiss Pilatus PC-9, replaced America's Cessna 'Tweet' and Turbo Mentor trainers in the 2010s and flies under the nickname 'Efroni' in Israel — which aircraft?
Beechcraft T-6 Texan II: Single-engine, low-wing tandem-seat turboprop military training aircraft.

Despite its name, this snake is actually grey to dark brown — the name instead describes the dark interior of its mouth, displayed as a threat — which species, the second-longest venomous snake after the king cobra?
Black mamba: Species of venomous snake. The black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis) is a species of highly venomous snake belonging to the family Elapidae.
Cattle, bison, buffalo, and goat-antelopes like sheep and goats all belong to this family of cloven-hoofed ruminants with over 140 living species — what is it?
Bovidae: Family of mammals belonging to even-toed ungulates.
Historically hardware-dependent in size, ranging anywhere from 1 to 48 bits, this unit of digital information now almost always means eight bits — what's it called?
Byte: Unit of digital information, usually 8 bits.
With the formula H2CO3, this fleeting compound has a lifespan of only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature before converting to water and carbon dioxide — which compound?
Carbonic acid: Chemical compound. The molecule rapidly converts to water and carbon dioxide in the presence of water.
Nicknamed 'no-see-ums' for their tiny 1-3mm size, these biting midges are also among the best-studied pollinators of cocoa plants — what is this fly family called?
Ceratopogonidae: Family of flies commonly known as no see ums, or biting midges.
Usually triggered when a gallstone blocks the cystic duct, this inflammatory condition causes right-upper abdominal pain that radiates to the shoulder — what is it?
Their 'lady' actually refers to the Virgin Mary, and their cheerful red-and-black warning colours tell predators they taste terrible — what is this 6,000-species family of small beetles?
Coccinellidae: Family of beetles. The more than 6,000 described species have a global distribution and are found in a variety of habitats.
First created near Darmstadt in 1996 and named for an astronomer on his 537th anniversary, this synthetic element (number 112) is so volatile it may even be a gas — which element?
Copernicium: Chemical element with atomic number 112 (Cn)
First flown in 1938 and built almost 14,000 strong at a factory in Buffalo, New York, this WWII fighter-bomber was known to British and Soviet pilots as the Tomahawk or Kittyhawk — which aircraft?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: American WWII fighter. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Spread by mosquitoes in tropical regions, this virus is often mild but can turn severe with bleeding, plummeting platelet counts, and dangerously low blood pressure — what is it?
Synthesized from L-DOPA in the brain and kidneys, this catecholamine acts as a neurotransmitter and drives a major brain pathway tied to reward and motivation — what is it?
Dopamine: Organic chemical that functions both as a hormone and a neurotransmitter.
Belonging to the order Anguilliformes and comprising roughly 1,000 species, these ray-finned predators transform dramatically from larva to adult and mostly live in salt water — what are they?
This fungal genus growing on rye and other cereals produces alkaloids that cause a poisoning condition in humans and livestock who eat contaminated grain — which group of fungi?
Ergot: Fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).

Its mating has never once been observed in the wild, and its five life stages were once mistaken for five separate species — this critically endangered fish is threatened by dams and overfishing. What is it?
European eel: Species of fish. The five stages of their development were originally thought to be different species.
When fibroblasts overproduce collagen after repeated injury or chronic inflammation, this permanent connective-tissue scarring can impair an organ's normal function — what is it called?
Fibrosis: Excess connective tissue in healing.
Known for wood used in tool handles, electric guitars, and Morgan Motor Company's sports car frames, this tree genus produced nymphs called the Meliae in Greek myth — which genus?
Fraxinus: Genus of plants. The genus is widespread throughout much of Europe, Asia, and North America.
This scientific field measures Earth's precise shape, gravity, and orientation in space, underpinning satellite positioning systems and global mapping — which discipline?
Geodesy: Science of measuring the shape, orientation, and gravity of Earth.

Weighing up to 175 grams, this South American tarantula is the world's most massive spider — despite a name inspired by an 18th-century engraving of one eating a hummingbird, it rarely actually preys on birds. Which species?
Goliath birdeater: Species of tarantula from South America.

Caused by a retrovirus that attacks the immune system, this condition has no cure or vaccine — yet with antiretroviral treatment a person can now expect to live a normal life and die with the virus, not of it. What is it?
HIV/AIDS: Spectrum of conditions caused by HIV infection.

This 19th-century American economist argued in his bestseller 'Progress and Poverty' that a single tax on land values could build a fairer, more productive society — sparking a movement named for him. Who was he?
An American aviator and aerospace engineer who first made his name as a big-budget Hollywood producer, this man grew famous late in life for his reclusive, eccentric ways — who was the magnate?
Howard Hughes: American aviator, aerospace engineer and business magnate (1905–1976)
This family of long-legged wading birds that live in wetlands and forests lent its name — mistakenly — to the scientific name of the western cattle egret in 1757 — what's the bird group called?
Ibis: Long-legged wading birds with down-curved beaks.
Sold under the brand name Accutane, this vitamin A-related retinoid treats severe cystic acne but commonly causes dry lips, dry skin, and increased sunburn risk — what is it called?
Isotretinoin: Medication primarily used to treat severe acne.
This German craftsman's mechanical printing press — with its oil-based ink and adjustable metal type — sparked an information revolution that helped fuel the Renaissance and Reformation — who is he?
Johannes Gutenberg: German inventor and craftsman (c. 1393–1406 – 1468)
This Canadian atmospheric scientist holds a chair in public policy at Texas Tech and in 2021 became chief scientist of the Nature Conservancy — who is she?
Katharine Hayhoe: Canadian atmospheric scientist. Katharine Anne Scott Hayhoe (born 1972) is a Canadian atmospheric scientist.
He served as U.S. Treasury Secretary, ran the National Economic Council, and was the 27th president of Harvard before resigning his professorship there in 2026. Which economist is this?
Named after the Italian word for lemon, this citrus-scented compound comes in two mirror-image forms — one smelling of oranges, the other like pine — what is it?

Born into one of Europe's richest families in Vienna, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge before giving away his inheritance and enlisting in the Austro-Hungarian Army — who is he?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Austrian philosopher and logician (1889–1951)
Grown as the source of the tropical mango fruit, this evergreen tree in the cashew family can reach 30 meters tall and comes in two genetic types — what species is it?
Mangifera indica: Species of flowering plant in the cashew family Anacardiaceae.

First synthesized near Darmstadt in 1982, this fleeting synthetic element — its most stable isotope lasts mere seconds — was named for the Austrian-Swedish nuclear physicist Lise Meitner. Which element is it?
Meitnerium: Chemical element with atomic number 109 (Mt)
Sitting atop the brainstem and linking it to the diencephalon and cerebrum, this structure governs vision, hearing, motor control, and arousal -- what is it called?
Midbrain: Forward-most portion of the brainstem.
The platypus and the four species of echidna are the only living mammals in this order that lay eggs rather than bear live young — what is it called?
Made by giving a paper loop a half-twist before joining the ends, this non-orientable surface first appeared in Roman mosaics — what is it called?
Möbius strip: Non-orientable surface with one edge.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandins, though it carries a notable risk of liver problems — what is it?
Nimesulide: Anti-inflammatory drug. Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.

The type species that gives its name to the Oleaceae family of lilac, jasmine, and ash, this Mediterranean evergreen bears a fruit classed botanically as a drupe — like a cherry or peach — what is it?
Also known as jícama or Mexican turnip, this pea-family vine's edible tuberous root comes in a milky-juice form and a watery-juice form — which species is it?
Pachyrhizus erosus: Species of legume. Pachyrhizus tuberosus and Pachyrhizus ahipa are the other two cultivated species in the genus.
Whose name comes from Greek words for 'congealed' and 'curdled' — this plant-cell-wall polymer is extracted from citrus as a powder that makes jams and jellies set?
Pectin: Structural carbohydrate in the cell walls of land plants and some algae.
Grouped within the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, this genus contains today's living flamingo species — which genus?
First synthesized in 1940 by bombarding uranium-238 with deuterons at UC Berkeley, this radioactive metal can expand up to 70% in volume when its surface oxidizes — which element?
Plutonium: Chemical element with atomic number 94 (Pu)
Though often mistaken for a true antelope, this hoofed North American mammal is actually the last living member of its own family, and its closest relatives are the giraffe and okapi — which animal?

Pronghorn: Species of North American hoofed mammal. The pronghorn (UK:, US:) (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.
Named for its four heads, this large muscle group covers the front of the thigh and is the sole muscle that extends the knee — what is it?
Quadriceps: Group of human leg muscle.

Nicknamed the 'Jug,' this WWII American fighter-bomber carried eight .50-caliber machine guns and weighed up to eight tons fully loaded, making it one of the heaviest fighters of the war — which aircraft?

Republic P-47 Thunderbolt: Family of fighter aircraft. The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (nicknamed the "Jug") is a World War II-era fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 through 1945.

A Mediterranean shrub in the mint family, this plant bears fragrant, needle-like evergreen leaves and purple, white, pink, or blue flowers — and those leaves are a beloved cooking flavoring. What is it?
Rosemary: Species of plant. It has numerous cultivars, and its leaves are commonly used as a flavoring.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
